Product Documentation

Sample Product Requirement Briefs

For each Axis Connect enhancement, Hanna authors a structured requirement document before any developer work begins, capturing the objective, expected outcome, logic flow, and decision rules. Three representative briefs are shown below; all active work is tracked in ClickUp across two lists: Axis Connect (app-side) and CMS.

Daily Operations Metric Dashboard
CMS Live
Objective
Create a real-time Daily Operations Dashboard in CMS to provide immediate visibility of session compliance and operational performance, replacing manual daily report compilation across scattered sources.
Expected Outcome
Operations Team can monitor daily compliance health from a single CMS screen without consolidating reports manually. Abnormal sessions surface automatically in an exceptions section for immediate follow-up.
9 Dashboard Metrics Specified
Total classes conducted per day (with programme and role breakdowns)
RAC Submission Tracking: total expected, received, pending
Arrival Declaration Tracking: declared vs not declared
Acknowledgement Tracking: by reminder type (1-day and 2-hour)
Class Start Status: started vs not started
Class End Status: properly ended vs no End Class submission
Audit Tracking: conducted, with findings, issue categories
Cancelled Classes: breakdown by timing and initiator
Operational Exceptions: attendance overages, out-of-radius starts, missing submissions, late arrivals, no-ack cases, incident reports
UI Specification
Summary KPI cards at top · Charts and trends for submission and compliance rates · Exceptions table at bottom · Clickable metrics drill down into affected sessions and users · Date selector, programme category filter, and instructor/facilitator filter
Visualization
Overlapping Session Conflict Prevention
CMS Pending: Demo First
Objective
Prevent the same user from being tagged or assigned to two sessions with overlapping dates and times, regardless of whether the assignment is manual, via the app, CMS, or automated matching.
Expected Outcome
A user should never appear in two simultaneously running sessions. The system displays a scheduling conflict warning with the conflicting session details (session ID, programme, date, time) and blocks the assignment if overlap is confirmed.
Two-Layer Validation Design
Layer 1 (existing, unchanged): 2-hour proximity warning: soft alert, admin can choose to proceed
Layer 2 (new, hard block): Actual time overlap check runs after Layer 1; blocks assignment if sessions physically overlap
Back-to-back sessions (end time = new start time) remain allowed
Cross-midnight sessions handled using actual start/end datetime, not just date comparison
Validation applies to all assignment paths: admin manual, user self-booking, automated matching, future bot auto-assignment
Overlap Condition
Existing session start < New session end
AND existing session end > New session start
FAQ Management Module (CMS) + FAQ Module (App)
Both CMS: Production Release App: In Review
Objective
Create an FAQ management module in CMS so admins can create, update, and publish FAQ content without requiring a new app release. The content is retrieved directly in the Axis Connect app so users can self-serve answers to common questions.
Expected Outcome
Users can browse and search FAQs in-app, reducing direct admin contact for common issues. The Admin Team maintains the full knowledge base centrally from CMS. FAQ content is structured to support future use as a knowledge source for the AI chatbot.
Dependencies Identified
CMS FAQ Management Module must be completed and API connection to Axis Connect established before the app module can retrieve content
FAQ database schema must be structured for potential future chatbot knowledge base ingestion
Admin team to agree on category taxonomy and initial content before CMS build begins
Future Consideration
FAQ content database to serve as a structured knowledge source for the planned CMS AI chatbot, enabling the bot to pull from maintained, admin-curated content rather than unstructured text.

Systems & Automation

Production Google Apps Script Systems

AI-assisted development (Claude): specified the full business logic and requirements for two recurring manual monthly processes, then iteratively tested and reviewed results until every execution ran correctly, replacing them with live, maintained automation.

CMS Import Generator
Automation Live & Maintained
Objective
Replace a fully manual monthly process of consolidating session data from 10+ separate programme schedule spreadsheets (HWE, AKG, CPAP, QUICKHIIT, AFP, MOE, TWSH, and others) into a single values-only XLSX import file for the CMS.
System Design
Programme-specific business rules applied per source: job grouping by location, workout, day, and time; role-based rate tables; location database lookups
Workout-intensity-based capacity calculation: every workout type is classified High/Moderate/Low, and session participant capacity is set to the lower of venue capacity or instructor count × a per-instructor limit for that intensity
The QUICKHIIT module handles both face-to-face and virtual session variants from a single script, each producing its own XLSX against a separate import template
Modular, config-driven architecture: separate rule modules per programme, externalised spreadsheet IDs and column mappings so new programmes can be added without touching core logic
Diagnostic preview, error log, and historical output log built in for traceability before each import
Data Flow
Output Preview Mockup · sample data
Each run reads the schedule of every programme, each kept in its own spreadsheet, applies that programme's rules, and writes a preview tab per programme before anything is exported. Rows that need a fix are flagged, every run is logged, and the final file is a values-only XLSX in the CMS import template. Mock-up of the real layout, built with sample values.

HPB Audit Findings Generator
Automation Live & Maintained
Objective
Replace a fully manual matching process for the monthly HPB audit findings submission, where findings from a Google Form had to be cross-checked by hand against the audit schedule.
System Design
Matches submitted findings against the audit schedule by session ID, or by date, workout, and time for virtual sessions with no fixed session ID, with a fallback match when exactly one session of that workout ran that day
Auto-flags sessions missing findings and excludes cancelled or removed sessions from the match set
Populates the director's HPB submission template directly, removing the manual compilation step entirely

Flagship Enhancements

Five of the 65 Shipped Initiatives

The platform's highest-impact improvements, each defined by Hanna and coordinated through to production.

01
Automated Escalation & Cover System
Shipped
Problem

Chasing unacknowledged sessions and no-shows was manual and time-sensitive.

Solution

Cascading alert engine: 3-hour pre-class reminder, auto-calls at 1-day and 2-hour windows, 20-minute "class not started" alert.

Impact

Escalation runs on a clock, not a person watching a spreadsheet.

02
Geo-Fenced Safety & Compliance
Shipped
Problem

Trainers could mark "arrived" without being on-site. Safety conditions weren't captured.

Solution

Geo-tagging that locks "I Have Arrived" to a physical radius check, plus mandatory heat stress and haze declarations per session.

Impact

Verified on-site presence and a documented safety trail for every session.

03
Audit & Quality Assurance Module
Shipped
Problem

Audit observations lived in scattered notes with no consistent structure.

Solution

Structured Audit Findings module: auditor name, session reference, lapse severity, star ratings on trainer profile.

Impact

Standardised quality data with a faster path from flagged issue to coordinator action.

04
Intelligent Job Assignment
Shipped
Problem

Filling vacant jobs risked double-booking or assigning uncertified trainers.

Solution

Automated matching layer weighing tiering, site familiarity, urgency, certifications, and availability (with overlap blocking).

Impact

Faster, more reliable cover fills with built-in eligibility checks.

05
Operational Intelligence Dashboard
Shipped
Problem

The daily operations report was compiled manually across scattered sources.

Solution

CMS Dashboard 2.0 and a Daily Operations Metric Dashboard consolidating live acknowledgement, attendance, audit, and cancellation data.

Impact

Real-time management visibility, replacing a manual daily compilation with a live, always-current view.

Design Quality Assurance

Figma UI/UX Audit & AI-Agent Review Workflow

Beyond product requirements, Hanna runs structured design QA passes on the team's Figma reference files, then routes findings into an AI design agent as prioritized natural-language prompts rather than editing every screen by hand.

Multi-Flow UI/UX Reference Audit
Design QA Fixes In Progress
Starting Point
Before Hanna took over this product, the trainer app had only a basic session reminder, an unreliable certificate upload flow, no invoice visibility on the profile page, no location/map extraction on sessions, and no FAQ, incident report, or audit findings modules at all. The admin portal itself was non-functional, crashing on login. All of these were designed and built out after taking over the app.
Objective
Review the current 60+ screen Figma reference file spanning trainer, admin, and auditor journeys for UI/UX consistency, data-integrity gaps, and component reuse issues, then convert findings into a prioritized action list.
Method
Screen-by-screen visual audit across every flow in the file, cross-checked against the shared component library
Findings split by severity and by owner: cosmetic fixes handled hands-on to build Figma fluency; systemic issues batched into natural-language prompts for the file's AI design agent
Each agent run verified against a fresh screenshot before sign-off, rather than trusting the agent's own change summary
Representative Findings
Unfilled template placeholder text present across roughly a third of admin- and auditor-facing screens, never replaced with realistic sample content
A broken calculated field (duration not reflecting the set start/end times) paired with leftover internal test copy on a live session-detail screen
Rating inputs defaulting to a pre-filled value instead of an empty state, risking an unintended score being read as submitted
Inconsistent header icon and overflow handling between screens sharing the same underlying component
Outcome
Findings consolidated into a single batched prompt set for the next AI-agent session, with a separate flag for replacing any residual real personal data in sample content with fictional equivalents before the file is shared externally. Workflow is designed to repeat on future review passes.
Quality Assurance

Monthly App Check: A Repeatable Regression Checklist

A structured test checklist, designed by Hanna and run every month against the live app and CMS, so regressions and gaps in newly launched features are caught by the team before users find them.

Monthly App & CMS Regression Check
App + CMS Run Monthly
Objective
Confirm that core app and CMS behaviour still works after each release cycle, and that newly launched features behave as specified, using one fixed checklist so results can be compared month to month. Hanna designed the checklist, and she runs it every month alongside the operations team.
Structure
Four monthly rounds recorded between November 2025 and March 2026, roughly 34 check items per round
Each item carries a plain-language instruction a team member can follow with a test account, a status (Pass, Issue Occurred, Reviewing, Not ready), free-text remarks, and the tester's name
Six categories: App Functionality, Security & Compliance, System Stability & Performance, Data Sync & CMS Dashboard, User Management, and Upcoming Feature QA for features that have launched
Examples of What It Catches
Business-rule gaps: a restriction that blocks a user in the app but can still be bypassed from the admin side
Automation that does not trigger: a status that should change automatically after a period of inactivity but stays unchanged
Output mismatches: a generated report that drops a field the form captured
Cross-checks between the app and CMS, such as confirming a submission or timestamp in one appears correctly in the other
How Results Are Used
Items marked Issue Occurred are recorded with remarks for follow-up. Items marked Not ready stay on the list until the feature is released, so the same checklist doubles as a release-readiness view.
ChartCheck item status by monthly round
PassIssue occurredNot readyReviewingNot recorded
Each bar is one round of the same checklist. Items marked Not ready are features still in review, which stay on the list until they launch. February and March returned identical results.
ChartCheck items by category across the four rounds
Where the checklist spends its coverage: app behaviour and newly launched features first, then security and compliance rules.
